chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Zayd, from his father who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Isa ibn Abdullah al-Qummi entered. He welcomed him and brought him near to his seat. Then he said: 'O Isa ibn Abdullah! He is not from us, and there is no prestige for the one who was in a city wherein were one hundred thousand or more, and in that city there was one who was more devout than him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the criterion for spiritual prestige and being 'from us' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines spiritual nobility not by worldly prominence or wealth, but by comparative piety (*awra'*), specifically modesty and God-consciousness. He establishes that if any individual in a city of significant population possesses greater piety than you, you cannot claim the exclusive rank of 'from us' in terms of spiritual superiority, emphasizing humility over social status. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *fiqh al-awra'* (understanding one's spiritual shortcomings) as the true metric of closeness to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Abu Zayd, from his father who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Isa Bin Abdullah Al-Qummy came over. So he<sup>asws</sup> welcomed him and seated him near to him<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Isa Bin Abdullah! He is not from us, and there is no prestige, the one who was in a city wherein were one hundred thousand or more, and in that city there was one who was more devout than him’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn abu Zayd from his father who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) when ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Qumi came to see him. The Imam greeted him and gave him a seat near his own seat. The Imam then said, ‘O ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah, one is not from our people, and it is not an honor that one lives in a city of a hundred thousand people and someone else (one who is not a Shi ’a) therein excercises more restraint from worldly matters (sins) than he (a Shi’a) does.’”
